A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GenExam work, with 31 pages and Appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific text, figures, tables, and appendix material are fully comparable.

before.justification: v3 reports original model evaluations on GenExam, human-alignment experiments, and evaluator ablations in Tables 2–9.

after.justification: v4 retains the original GenExam evaluations, human-alignment results, and evaluator ablations in Tables 2–9.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Appendices B and E retain the same curation and evaluation procedures, GPT-5 judge, reference-image inputs, scoring points, and strict/relaxed scoring rules.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,000-sample benchmark across ten subjects, GenExam-Mini subset, image types, and four-level taxonomy. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario changes.

E2.justification: The generation-model configurations in Table 2, metric comparators in Table 3, evaluator alternatives in Table 4, and comparison sets in the remaining appendix tables are identical.

E3.justification: Both retain default generation configurations, GPT-5 with low reasoning effort, identical evaluation metrics, and the same sampling and human-rating procedures, including five experts evaluating 250 GPT-Image-1 images.

E4.justification: Evaluator, reference-input, and reasoning-effort ablations in Appendix C.1 are unchanged. The difficulty/type analyses, human-alignment checks, and error cases in Section 4.4 and Appendices C and F also match.

E5.justification: Human-rating aggregation, correlation tests, p-value and significance reporting in Tables 3–4, and standard deviations in Table 5 are unchanged. No run-count or seed information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match, including Tables 2–9 and Appendix F. Table 2 retains overall strict scores of 72.7% for Nano Banana Pro and 43.2% for GPT-Image-1.5.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions and mathematical content are identical. No formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims concerning multidisciplinary drawing exams, fine-grained evaluation, benchmark difficulty, and the gap between open-source and closed-source models.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix C preserve the same interpretations of rendering failures, reference-image benefits, evaluator limitations, and human alignment. No substantive explanation or applicability qualification changes.

D1.justification: Curation instructions, prompt templates, inference settings, evaluator cost/time information, and benchmark/code access information are identical. The arXiv stamp links to the corresponding version, without changing research-resource access.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to concept-illustration benchmarks and existing multidisciplinary evaluations is identical.

P1.justification: v4 replaces the running header 'Submission and Formatting Instructions for ICML 2026' with 'GenExam' and updates the preprint date and arXiv version/date stamp. Body prose, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–13, Tables 1–9, and the appendix taxonomy retain identical formatting and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the visible differences are confined to header/date/version wording.

improvement.justification: Replacing the irrelevant template header with 'GenExam' provides a small cosmetic cleanup. The main text and appendices otherwise retain identical methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and visual presentation, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
